styles.label: Culture
styles.blurb: Museums, the Islamic Art park and Souq Waqif lanes.

styles.label: History
styles.blurb: Old Doha, forts and the story of pearl diving.

styles.label: Family
styles.blurb: Beaches, parks and the aquarium at Katara.

stays.why: Modern towers and the Corniche on the doorstep; easy metro to the airport and sights.
Sleep in the old heart: market lanes, restaurants and the corniche walk at night.
Quiet new downtown next to Souq Waqif; main metro transfer at Msheireb station.
Marina living, cafés and a beach feel; good for longer stays and families.

food: Try Qatari dishes: machboos (spiced rice with meat or fish), harees and luqaimat dumplings with date syrup.
Souq Waqif is the easy first stop: grilled fish, Lebanese mezze and shisha courtyards in the evening.
Cheap eats: shawarma, karak tea and Indian or Pakistani cafeterias, often around QR 10–30 a meal.
Book a hotel brunch or a waterfront dinner at The Pearl or Katara for a special night.
Alcohol is served only in licensed hotel bars and restaurants. Dress modestly in public places.
more_time: Add a desert day: dune drive and Inland Sea views south of the city. Book a tour; check prices on the day.
Swap a city afternoon for Katara Cultural Village: beach, galleries and the mosque with blue tiles.
Take the metro to Education City for the National Library and campus architecture.

recommend.why: Two nights covers the museums, Souq Waqif and the Corniche without rushing; add a night for the desert or a beach day.

month_notes: Jan: mild days around 23°C, cool nights. Best month for walking the souq.
Feb: like January, a little warmer. Great for outdoor sights.
Mar: warming to 27°C. Comfortable mornings and evenings.
Apr: hot at 32°C by day. Do sights early, rest at midday.
May: 38°C and dry. Stick to malls, museums and the metro.
Jun: 41°C. Very hot. Go out only early or after sunset.
Jul: 41°C with humid nights. Indoor plans only.
Aug: as hot as July. Book hotels with pools.
Sep: still 39°C. Slightly easier evenings late in the month.
Oct: cooling to 35°C. Outdoor evenings become pleasant.
Nov: 30°C days, warm nights. Good all-round month.
Dec: 25°C days, cool nights. Peak season; book ahead.

climate_guide.summary: Hot desert climate: sunny nearly every day, very little rain, and a long, humid summer.

items.title: Best time: November to March
items.text: Days around 23–30°C with cool evenings. Ideal for the souq, Corniche and desert trips.

items.title: Summer is extreme (June to September)
items.text: Highs of 39–41°C. Plan indoor sights by day and go outside only at sunrise or after dark.

items.title: Humid by the water
items.text: Muggy evenings from May to October, especially on the Corniche and at The Pearl.

items.title: Almost no rain
items.text: Only a few short showers between December and March. No umbrella needed most of the year.

items.title: Occasional dust
items.text: Dusty winds can haze the sky and spoil desert views. Check the forecast before booking a dune trip.

items.title: What to pack
items.text: Light breathable clothes, a hat and strong sunscreen; a light layer for cold indoor AC and winter nights; modest clothing for mosques and souqs.

transit.best: Doha Metro for the main sights, with taxis or ride apps for the last stretch.

modes.text: Three lines (Red, Gold, Green); Msheireb is the main transfer station. About QR 2 per trip and QR 6 for a day pass; VIP cars cost more. Free metrolink buses connect stations to nearby areas.
Cheap but infrequent and often late; route maps are hard to read. Use the free metrolink feeder buses instead where you can.
Karwa and Al Million are the main taxis; Uber works well in Doha. Handy for the airport and late nights.
Driving is on the right. Traffic jams and roadworks are common, so allow extra time.
Only pleasant November to March, and sights are spread out. Use the metro or a taxi in summer.
A free tram runs in Lusail and Msheireb Downtown. Useful for short hops in those areas.
